statement: Tech shares had their worst week since 2020 as fears grew that huge AI spending will not pay off, and Nvidia fell sharply on Friday.
Gold fell to its lowest since September 2025 even while stocks crashed, and traders expect the Fed to raise rates in December.
The stock market's fear gauge will be lower on January 15, 2027 than at Friday's close near 36.
reasoning: The VIX closed near 36 on November 20 after the S&P 500 fell into a correction and Nvidia lost about 14 in a single day. Readings this high rarely last for weeks, because fear tends to fade once the selling slows, even when prices do not fully recover. I expect it well below 30 by mid-January. I am wrong if the VIX closes on January 15 above Friday's close, for example because the SEC look at Nvidia's accounting grows into a wider crisis or a Fed hike sets off another leg down.

statement: The US stock market (S&P 500) will close higher on June 30, 2027 than it closed on November 20, 2026.
reasoning: The S&P 500 closed November 20 more than 10 below its record, after a week of steep AI-driven losses and an expected Fed hike in December. Most corrections that stop short of a recession have recovered within seven months, and much of the bad news (the hike, Nvidia's troubles) is already in prices. I am wrong if the index ends June 2027 below Friday's close, for example because the Fed keeps raising rates into 2027 or the slump turns into a recession.

statement: The US dollar index will be higher on December 11, 2026 than at the November 20 close, after the Fed's December 8-9 meeting.

Higher US rates and a rush to safety during a stock slump both tend to lift the dollar. I am wrong if the dollar index is lower on December 11, for example because the Fed holds rates or signals that this hike is the last one, or because weak jobs data shift bets toward cuts.

statement: The dollar will buy fewer Japanese yen on December 31, 2026 than on November 20, 2026.

I am wrong if the dollar buys more yen at year end than on November 20, for example because the Bank of Japan holds rates or the Fed's hike widens the gap between US and Japanese rates.

statement: The Nikkei 225 will close lower on December 18, 2026, the day of the Bank of Japan decision, than on November 20, 2026.

I am wrong if the Nikkei closes December 18 above its November 20 close, for example because AI stocks bounce sharply or the Bank of Japan holds rates.

statement: Bitcoin will be cheaper on December 4, 2026 than on November 20, 2026.

statement: Coinbase shares will close lower on December 31, 2026 than on November 20, 2026.

statement: Brent crude oil will be cheaper on December 31, 2026 than its November 20 settlement near 92.57 dollars a barrel.

statement: US gasoline prices (UGA fund) will be lower on January 15, 2027 than on November 20, 2026.

statement: US homebuilder stocks (ITB) will close lower on December 31, 2026 than on November 20, 2026.

statement: Ether will be cheaper on December 11, 2026 than on November 23, 2026, when it traded near 1,740 dollars.

statement: One euro will buy fewer US dollars on December 18, 2026 than on November 23, 2026, when it bought about 1.10 dollars.

One Fed governor has even floated a bigger step. We are wrong if the euro is worth more than 1.10 dollars on December 18, for example because the Fed signals it will stop raising rates or the European bank hints at more rises.

statement: One British pound will buy fewer US dollars on December 18, 2026, the day after the Bank of England decision, than on November 23, 2026.

A smaller rise in Britain and a bigger one in the US both favour the dollar. Surveys also say British growth is cooling. We are wrong if the pound buys more dollars on December 18 than on November 23.

statement: US energy company stocks (XLE fund) will close lower on January 29, 2027 than on November 23, 2026.

statement: US natural gas prices (UNG fund) will be lower on December 18, 2026 than on November 23, 2026.

statement: The interest the US government pays to borrow money for 5 years will be higher on December 11, 2026 than at the November 23, 2026 close.

We are wrong if the 5-year rate is lower on December 11, for example because the inflation report out this Wednesday comes in soft or the Fed hints this is its last rise.

statement: Germany's DAX stock index will close higher on January 29, 2027 than on November 23, 2026, when it closed near 25,360 points.

statement: The Chinese stock market (Shanghai Composite) will close higher on January 29, 2027 than on November 23, 2026, when it was near 3,500 points.

statement: One US dollar will buy fewer Chinese yuan on December 31, 2026 than on November 23, 2026, when it bought about 6.66 yuan.

statement: One US dollar will buy fewer Swiss francs on March 19, 2027 than on November 23, 2026, when it bought about 0.84 francs.

statement: Arabica coffee will be cheaper on March 31, 2027 than on November 23, 2026, when it closed near 267 cents a pound.
reasoning: Brazil, the biggest grower, expects its arabica harvest to rise by about a third this year. Coffee stored in exchange warehouses is near a 27-year low, and El Niño, a warm Pacific weather pattern, could bring dry weather to Brazil. Either could push prices up. We are wrong if arabica is above 267 cents a pound on March 31, 2027.

statement: Wheat (Teucrium Wheat Fund) will be cheaper on December 31, 2026 than on November 23, 2026.

With the Fed set to raise rates on December 9, we expect the dollar to stay strong and wheat to drift lower to year end. We are wrong if the fund is higher on December 31, for example if foreign buying picks up or bad weather threatens a big crop elsewhere.

statement: US natural gas prices will be lower on January 29, 2027 than at today's close on November 23, 2026.

A long cold spell in December or January, or a jump in gas sent abroad by ship, would prove us wrong.

statement: US homebuilder stocks will be lower on February 26, 2027 than at today's close on November 23, 2026.

statement: The price of oil (Brent) will be lower on February 26, 2027 than at today's close on November 23, 2026.

statement: US power and water company stocks will be lower on February 26, 2027 than at today's close on November 23, 2026.

statement: The inflation investors expect over the next 5 years will be lower on January 29, 2027 than on November 23, 2026.

Oil, a big part of price rises, is about 18 in 100 below its October level, and forecasters see too much oil in 2027. Oil climbing back above 100 dollars a barrel, or the Fed holding off on a rate rise, would prove us wrong.

statement: One US dollar will buy fewer Japanese yen on January 29, 2027 than at today's close on November 23, 2026.

statement: The price of gold will be lower on December 11, 2026 than at today's close on November 23, 2026.

Higher rates make gold, which pays no interest, less attractive, and they lift the dollar, which makes gold dearer abroad. A bank analyst at ING expects gold to stay weak while rates and the dollar stay high. Gold above Monday's close on December 11, perhaps from central banks buying the dip or the Fed skipping the rate rise, would prove us wrong.

statement: One US dollar will buy more Canadian dollars on January 29, 2027 than at today's close on November 23, 2026.

Canada sells a lot of oil abroad, and oil is about 18 in 100 below its October level, with forecasters warning of too much oil in 2027. statement: The interest rate on 10-year US government bonds will be higher on December 18, 2026 than on November 24, 2026, after the Fed's meeting of December 9 and 10.
